$comment: Source of truth for the generated HTTP API reference. Run `node scripts/docs/gen-api-reference.mjs` after editing.

auth.description: Send your namespace token as a bearer token in the `Authorization` header. Every control plane request also requires the `namespace` query parameter. See [Authentication](/docs/api/authentication).

parameters.namespace: Name of the namespace to operate in.
parameters.limit: Maximum number of results to return.
parameters.cursor: Pagination cursor. Pass the `pagination.cursor` value from the previous response to fetch the next page.
parameters.pagination.cursor: Cursor for the next page, or `null` when there are no more results.
parameters.actor.name: Actor name as registered in your RivetKit registry.
parameters.actor.key: Actor key. Multi-part keys are joined with `/`, see [Actor Keys](/docs/api/actor-keys).
parameters.actor.namespace_id: ID of the namespace the actor belongs to.
parameters.actor.datacenter: Datacenter the actor is scheduled in.
parameters.actor.crash_policy: What happens when the actor crashes.
parameters.actors[].name: Actor name as registered in your RivetKit registry.
parameters.actors[].key: Actor key. Multi-part keys are joined with `/`, see [Actor Keys](/docs/api/actor-keys).
parameters.actors[].namespace_id: ID of the namespace the actor belongs to.
parameters.actors[].datacenter: Datacenter the actor is scheduled in.
parameters.actors[].crash_policy: What happens when the actor crashes.
parameters.created: `true` if this request created the actor, `false` if it already existed.
parameters.names: Map of actor name to metadata.
parameters.names.metadata: Free-form metadata attached to the actor name.
parameters.token: The issued token. Treat it as a secret.
parameters.issued_ts: When the token was issued, in Unix milliseconds.
parameters.expires_ts: When the token expires, in Unix milliseconds.
parameters.namespace_id: ID of the namespace the token is scoped to.
parameters.subject: Subject attached to the token, if any.
parameters.grants[].resource: Resource type the grant applies to.
parameters.grants[].target: `"any"` for every resource of this type, or `{ "id": "..." }` for one resource.
parameters.grants[].operations: Operations the token may perform on the target.
parameters.update_ts: When the key was last written, in Unix milliseconds.

auth.description: Send a token in the `x-rivet-token` header, inline in the path as `{actor_id}@{token}`, or in the `rvt-token` query parameter. Use a public token (`pk_`) from browsers and a secret token (`sk_`) from trusted backends. See [Authentication](/docs/api/authentication).

parameters.actor: Actor ID, actor ID with an inline token (`{actor_id}@{token}`), or actor name combined with the `rvt-*` query parameters.
parameters.rvt-namespace: Namespace the actor lives in. Required when `{actor}` is an actor name.
parameters.rvt-method: How to resolve an actor name to an actor. `getOrCreate` requires `rvt-pool`.
parameters.rvt-key: Actor key. Separate multi-part keys with commas. Deprecated in favor of `rvt-key-part`, which unambiguously represents a component containing a literal comma.
parameters.rvt-key-part: Actor key component. Repeat this parameter once per key component instead of comma-joining them into `rvt-key`. Takes precedence over `rvt-key` when both are present.
parameters.rvt-pool: Pool to create the actor on when `rvt-method=getOrCreate`. RivetKit registers the `default` pool unless configured otherwise.
parameters.rvt-input: Base64url-encoded CBOR input passed to `createState` and `onCreate` when `rvt-method=getOrCreate` creates the actor.
parameters.rvt-region: Preferred region when `rvt-method=getOrCreate` creates the actor.
parameters.rvt-crash-policy: Crash policy when `rvt-method=getOrCreate` creates the actor. RivetKit defaults to `sleep`.
parameters.rvt-skip-ready-wait: Return as soon as the actor is resolved instead of waiting for it to be ready.
parameters.rvt-token: Token to authenticate with. Prefer the `x-rivet-token` header or inline path token when possible.
parameters.args: Positional arguments passed to the action, in order.
parameters.output: Value returned by the action. `null` if the action returned `undefined`.

inspector.description: Inspector endpoints do not accept namespace tokens. Send the actor's inspector token as a bearer token in the `Authorization` header. Each actor generates its own inspector token on first start and stores it in its KV storage under the single byte `0x03`. Read it through the control plane with `GET /actors/{actor_id}/kv/keys/Aw==?namespace={namespace}` using a namespace token; the response `value` is the token, base64-encoded. The dashboard does this for you.

groups.api: Malformed requests to the control plane.
groups.connection: Actor connections opened through the connection protocol.
groups.guard: The gateway that routes requests to actors, including request parsing, rate limits, and timeouts.
groups.kv: Low-level KV storage inside an actor.
groups.protocol: Encoding and framing of connection protocol messages.
groups.user: Errors thrown by your actor code. The code is whatever you pass to `UserError`.
groups.ws: WebSocket handling for the connection protocol and `onWebSocket` handlers.

endpoints.title: List Actors
endpoints.description: List actors in a namespace, optionally filtered by name, key, or ID. Results are paginated.
endpoints.notes: `key` requires `name`. `actor_id` cannot be combined with `name` or `key`. Destroyed actors are excluded unless `include_destroyed` is `true`.

parameters.name: Only return actors with this name.
parameters.key: Only return the actor with this key. Requires `name`. Multi-part keys are joined with `/`, see [Actor Keys](/docs/api/actor-keys).
parameters.actor_id: Only return actors with these IDs. Repeat the parameter for multiple IDs.
parameters.include_destroyed: Include actors that have been destroyed.

responses.200: Matching actors and a cursor for the next page. `pagination.cursor` is `null` on the last page.

endpoints.title: Create Actor
endpoints.description: Create a new actor. Fails if an actor with the same name and key already exists.
endpoints.notes: Prefer [Get or Create Actor](/docs/api/actors/get-or-create) for idempotent access by key. Use this endpoint when you need a fresh actor every time, for example with a random key.

parameters.name: Name of the actor as registered in your RivetKit registry.
parameters.key: Key identifying this actor within its name. Multi-part keys are joined with `/`, see [Actor Keys](/docs/api/actor-keys). Omit for a keyless actor.
parameters.runner_name_selector: Pool that runs the actor. RivetKit registers the `default` pool unless configured otherwise.
parameters.crash_policy: What happens when the actor crashes. RivetKit defaults to `sleep`.
parameters.datacenter: Datacenter to create the actor in. Defaults to the datacenter serving the request.
parameters.input: Base64url-encoded CBOR input passed to the actor's `createState` and `onCreate` hooks.

endpoints.title: Get or Create Actor
endpoints.description: Return the actor with the given name and key, creating it if it does not exist. This is the HTTP equivalent of client.actor.getOrCreate(key).
endpoints.notes: The response includes `created`, which is `true` when this call created the actor. Gateway endpoints can perform the same lookup inline with the `rvt-*` selector parameters, so you only need this endpoint when you want the `actor_id` up front.

parameters.name: Name of the actor as registered in your RivetKit registry.
parameters.key: Key identifying this actor within its name. Multi-part keys are joined with `/`, see [Actor Keys](/docs/api/actor-keys).
parameters.runner_name_selector: Pool that runs the actor. RivetKit registers the `default` pool unless configured otherwise.
parameters.crash_policy: What happens when the actor crashes. RivetKit defaults to `sleep`.
parameters.datacenter: Datacenter to create the actor in if it does not exist. Defaults to the datacenter serving the request.
parameters.input: Base64url-encoded CBOR input passed to the actor's `createState` and `onCreate` hooks when the actor is created.

endpoints.title: Destroy Actor
endpoints.description: Destroy an actor. The actor's onDestroy hook runs, then its state is deleted permanently.

endpoints.title: Sleep Actor
endpoints.description: Put an actor to sleep. The actor runs its shutdown sequence and persists its state, then wakes on the next request.

endpoints.title: Reschedule Actor
endpoints.description: Move an actor to a different worker. The actor runs its shutdown sequence, then restarts elsewhere with its persisted state.

endpoints.title: List Actor Names
endpoints.description: List the distinct actor names that have been created in a namespace.

endpoints.title: Call Action
endpoints.description: Invoke an action defined on an actor and return its result. This is the HTTP equivalent of calling a method on an actor handle in the RivetKit client.
endpoints.notes: Arguments are passed as a JSON array in `args` and spread into the action's parameters. The action's return value comes back in `output`. Actions that return `undefined` respond with `{ "output": null }`.

parameters.action: Name of the action as defined in the actor's `actions` map.

endpoints.title: Raw HTTP Request
endpoints.description: Forward a raw HTTP request to an actor's onRequest handler. The method, headers, body, and the path after /request/ are passed through unchanged.
endpoints.notes: Use this when an actor exposes its own HTTP routes, streams responses (for example Server-Sent Events), or needs to accept non-JSON payloads. The response is whatever the actor's `onRequest` handler returns.

parameters.path: Path forwarded to the actor. The actor sees a request whose URL path is `/{path}`.

responses.200: The response returned by the actor's `onRequest` handler.

endpoints.title: Check Health
endpoints.description: Check that an actor is reachable through the gateway. Resolves the actor, waits for it to be ready unless rvt-skip-ready-wait is set, and returns a plain-text ok.

responses.200: The actor is running and reachable. Body is the text `ok`.

endpoints.title: Send Queue Message
endpoints.description: Enqueue a durable message for an actor. Optionally wait for the actor to complete it and return a response.
endpoints.notes: By default, the request returns after the message is enqueued. Set `wait` to `true` to wait for `message.complete(...)`; `timeout` sets that wait in milliseconds, and a timeout returns `status: "timedOut"` without canceling the queued work.

parameters.name: Name of the queue message as defined in the actor's `queues` map.

responses.200: The message was enqueued, with its completion status when waiting.

endpoints.title: Get Runtime Metadata
endpoints.description: Identify the RivetKit runtime serving an actor.

responses.200: Runtime name, version, and runtime type.

protocol.title: Connect
protocol.description: Open a persistent WebSocket connection to an actor. One connection carries action calls, event subscriptions, and errors as JSON messages, which is what handle.connect() does in the RivetKit client.
protocol.notes:
`{actor}` accepts the same forms as every gateway endpoint: an actor ID, `{actor_id}@{token}`, or an actor name with `rvt-*` query parameters. See [Actor Routing](/docs/api/actor-routing).

Connection options travel as WebSocket subprotocols in the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` header because browsers cannot set arbitrary headers on an upgrade. Always include `rivet`, then add any of the prefixed entries below.

| Subprotocol | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `rivet` | Required. Lets servers that insist on a matching protocol accept the upgrade. |
| `rivet_encoding.json` | Message encoding. `json` is the default and is documented here. The RivetKit client uses `cbor` or `bare`; the payloads are the same, only the framing differs. |
| `rivet_token.{token}` | Token to authenticate with. See [WebSocket Requests](/docs/api/authentication#websocket-requests). |
| `rivet_conn_params.{params}` | Optional connection parameters passed to the actor's `createConnState` and `onBeforeConnect` hooks, as URL-encoded JSON. |
| `rivet_skip_ready_wait` | Complete the upgrade as soon as the actor is resolved instead of waiting for it to be ready. |

Every message in both directions is a JSON object of the form `{ "body": { "tag": "<Message>", "val": { ... } } }`. The server sends `Init` first; nothing else arrives before it. There is no ping or heartbeat message. Rely on WebSocket ping frames or your own timeout to detect a dead connection.

sections.title: Handshake
sections.notes: After the upgrade completes, the server sends `Init` before any other message. Store `connectionId` if you need to correlate connection-scoped state; nothing else needs to be sent before calling actions or subscribing to events.

sections.title: Actions
sections.notes:
Send an `ActionRequest` with a client-chosen `id`. The server answers with an `ActionResponse` carrying the same `id`, or with an [`Error`](#errors) whose `actionId` matches. Requests may be pipelined; responses are not guaranteed to arrive in order, so match on `id` rather than position.

This is the connection equivalent of [Call Action](/docs/api/gateway/call-action) over HTTP. Actions called on a connection can also read connection state set in `createConnState`.

sections.title: Events
sections.notes:
Send a `SubscriptionRequest` with `subscribe: true` to start receiving `Event` messages for an event name, and `subscribe: false` to stop. Subscriptions are per connection and are lost when the connection closes, so resubscribe after reconnecting. The server does not acknowledge subscription changes. If the actor rejects a subscription, the connection is closed with the error as the close reason.

Events sent by the actor to a connection that has not subscribed to that event name are dropped.

sections.title: Errors
sections.notes:
Errors on an established connection arrive as `Error` messages. `actionId` is set when the error answers a specific `ActionRequest` and `null` for connection-level errors such as a malformed message. The `group` and `code` values are the same ones the HTTP API returns; see [Error Codes](/docs/api/error-codes).

Errors that prevent the connection from being established, such as an invalid token or an actor that does not exist, are reported by closing the WebSocket with a reason of the form `{group}.{code}#{ray_id}`. See [WebSockets](/docs/api/websockets#close-codes).

fields.Init.actorId: ID of the actor this connection is attached to.
fields.Init.connectionId: ID of this connection. Matches `c.conn.id` inside the actor.
fields.ActionRequest.id: Client-chosen identifier used to match the response. Any integer that is unique among in-flight requests on this connection.
fields.ActionRequest.name: Name of the action as defined in the actor's `actions` map.
fields.ActionRequest.args: Positional arguments passed to the action, as a JSON array.
fields.ActionResponse.output: Value returned by the action. `null` if the action returned `undefined`.
fields.SubscriptionRequest.eventName: Name of the event as defined in the actor's `events` map.
fields.Event.name: Name of the event.
fields.Event.args: Arguments passed to `c.broadcast()` or `conn.send()`, as a JSON array.
fields.Error.group: Subsystem that produced the error, such as `actor`, `auth`, or `user`.
fields.Error.message: Human-readable explanation. Do not match on it.
fields.Error.metadata: Structured details attached by the actor or gateway, if any.
fields.Error.actionId: `id` of the `ActionRequest` this error answers, or `null` for connection-level errors.
fields.Error.actor: Actor that handled the message, when known.
fields.Error.actor.generation: Generation of the actor process. Increments each time the actor restarts.
fields.Error.actor.key: Key of the actor, if it has one.

children.title: Inspector
children.notes: These endpoints power the Rivet dashboard's actor inspector.

responses.401: The inspector token is missing or invalid.

responses.401: The inspector token is missing or invalid.

endpoints.title: Patch State
endpoints.description: Replace the actor's current state.
endpoints.notes: This writes state directly and bypasses actor actions. Use it only for inspection and recovery.

responses.401: The inspector token is missing or invalid.

endpoints.title: List Connections
endpoints.description: List the actor's active connections.

responses.401: The inspector token is missing or invalid.

endpoints.title: List Actions

responses.401: The inspector token is missing or invalid.

responses.200: Queue size, capacity, truncation status, and pending message metadata.

responses.200: Workflow history after scheduling the replay.

endpoints.title: Create Token
endpoints.description: Issue a scoped token. Use this to mint short-lived tokens that grant a client access to a single actor instead of sharing your namespace token.
endpoints.notes: Each grant names a resource type, a target (`"any"` or a specific `{ "id": ... }`), and the operations it allows. The RivetKit client wraps this as `handle.issueToken()`.

parameters.namespace: Namespace the token is valid in.
parameters.duration: Lifetime in seconds. Omit for the default lifetime.
parameters.subject: Free-form subject to attach to the token, such as a user ID.
parameters.grants[].resource: Resource type the grant applies to.
parameters.grants[].target: `"any"` for every resource of this type, or `{ "id": "..." }` for one resource.
parameters.grants[].operations: Operations the token may perform on the target.

endpoints.title: Inspect Token
endpoints.description: Return the namespace, grants, and expiry of the token used to authenticate the request.

endpoints.title: List Namespaces
endpoints.description: List namespaces, optionally filtered by name or ID. Results are paginated.
endpoints.notes: Use `namespace_id` for multiple IDs. `namespace_ids` is deprecated.

parameters.name: Only return namespaces with this name.
parameters.namespace_id: Only return namespaces with these IDs. Repeat the parameter for multiple IDs.

responses.200: Matching namespaces and a cursor for the next page.

endpoints.title: Create Namespace
endpoints.description: Create a namespace with a unique name and a display name.

parameters.name: Unique name used to identify the namespace.

endpoints.title: List Workers
endpoints.description: List workers connected to the control plane in a namespace, optionally filtered by name or key. Results are paginated.

parameters.name: Only return workers with this name.
parameters.envoy_key: Only return workers with these keys. Repeat the parameter for multiple keys.

responses.200: Matching workers and a cursor for the next page.

endpoints.title: List Worker Configs
endpoints.description: List worker configurations in a namespace, grouped by worker name and datacenter.
endpoints.notes: Filter by `variant` to return only `normal` or `serverless` configurations. Use `runner_name` for multiple names because `runner_names` is deprecated.

parameters.variant: Only return configurations with this variant.
parameters.runner_name: Only return configurations for these worker names. Repeat the parameter for multiple names.

responses.200: Worker configurations grouped by worker name and datacenter.

endpoints.title: Upsert Worker Config
endpoints.description: Create or replace a worker configuration in each specified datacenter.
endpoints.notes: A `normal` configuration controls workers with direct, persistent connections. A `serverless` configuration starts workers through a URL and requires `url` and `request_lifespan`. Configurations for omitted datacenters are deleted. A failure can occur after some datacenters have already changed.

parameters.runner_name: Name of the worker pool to configure.
parameters.datacenters: Map of datacenter names to worker configurations.

endpoints.title: Delete Worker Config
endpoints.description: Delete a worker configuration from every configured datacenter.
endpoints.notes: A failure can occur after the configuration has already been deleted from some datacenters.

parameters.runner_name: Name of the worker pool whose configuration will be deleted.

endpoints.title: Refresh Config Metadata
endpoints.description: Fetch and store fresh metadata for a serverless worker configuration.
endpoints.notes: The endpoint refreshes the first serverless configuration it finds across datacenters. It fails when the worker name has no serverless configuration.

parameters.runner_name: Name of the worker pool whose metadata will be refreshed.

endpoints.title: Serverless Health Check
endpoints.description: Probe a serverless URL and return the protocol version reported by its metadata endpoint.
endpoints.notes: Metadata fetch failures are returned as a `failure` result in a successful HTTP response.

parameters.headers: Headers to include in the metadata request.

responses.200: A success result with the reported version or a failure result with error details.

endpoints.title: Get Metadata
endpoints.description: Get build, runtime, compiler, and fleet protocol metadata for the control plane.
endpoints.notes: The protocol versions are the versions agreed on by the fleet, which can differ from the versions compiled into the responding node.

responses.200: Build and protocol metadata for the responding node and its fleet.

endpoints.title: List Datacenters
endpoints.description: List the datacenters configured for the control plane.

responses.200: Configured datacenters and an empty pagination cursor.
